name: compute_median
instruction: Make a RASP program that computes the median of the sequence. Example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] --> [3, 3, 3, 3, 3]; make_compute_median
ground_truth:
def fun(sequence):
    sorted_sequence = sorted(sequence)
    n = len(sequence)
    mid = n // 2
    if n % 2 == 0:  # even number of items
        median = (sorted_sequence[mid - 1] + sorted_sequence[mid]) / 2
    else:  # odd number of items
        median = sorted_sequence[mid]
    return [median] * n

name: wrap
instruction: Make a RASP program that wraps each element within a range (make the default range [2, 7]). Wrapping here means that the values are projected into the range starting from the lower bound, once they grow larger than the upper bound, they start again at the lower. Example: [1, 5, 8], range=[0, 5] --> [1, 0, 3]; make_wrap
ground_truth:
def wrap_into_range(min, max, x):
    # Calculate the size of the range
    range_size = max - min 
    # Wrap x into the range
    wrapped_x = ((x - min) % range_size) + min
    return wrapped_x



def fun(sequence, wrap_range=(2, 7)):
    return [wrap_into_range(wrap_range[0], wrap_range[1], i) for i in sequence]
